full_judgment: 5. Being aggrieved twenty-one tenants of the said building filed Title Suit No. 111 of 1974 before the then Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 for declarations and permanent injunction restraining the Government-defend-ants from evicting them from their respective flats and from interfering in any way with their peaceful possession. The suit was heard by the Munsif, Dhaka who after hearing the parties dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 31-1-1984, against the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 89 of 1984 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka which was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and after hearing the parties the said Court allowed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 27-1-1972 and restrained the Government and others to dispossess the plaintiffs from their respective flats subject to due process of law. But while the said suit was pending, the Government asked the tenants of the China Building to pay rents as per their tenancy agreements with their original landlords subject to the decision of the suit vide Memo No. SHA 10/lal-224/ 71/365 dated 5-5-1980. The further case of the petitioner is, that the petitioner has been in great trouble in the year 1973-1975 as his wife was murdered at his residence by the night-guard of the "China Building" in collaboration with the petitioner's domestic servant and when the petitioner was managing the affairs of the building as a caretaker, as such, there was default in payment of rent, and meanwhile the Certificate Officer issued a certificate Case No. 153 of 1981 dated 29-8-1981against the petitioner for realising the arrear rents. The petitioner prayed for exemption of the arrear rent and withdrawal of Certificate Case from the said Court by his letter dated 14-9-1981. In response to the aforesaid representation, the Government directed the General Certificate Officer to withdraw the said certificate case dated 26-9-1981 and by a subsequent Memo dated 11-5-1982 the respondent-Government directed the petitioner to pay arrear rents at the rate of Taka 275.00 per month from 1-1-1972 to 31-12-1980. Accordingly, the petitioner paid the arrear rents and on payment of rents on different occasions the petitioner informed the respondent about the payment of rent vide letter dated 4-10-1983, 31-1-2001, 5-1-2002 and lastly by letter dated 7-1-2003 and thus the petitioner paid rents Taka 1,00,600 upto 31-12-2003 and Taka 3,300 as rents for the period from 1-1-2003 to 31-12-2003. In the meantime, the petitioner paid Taka 5,050 as rents upto 31-12-1980 out of Taka 29,700 (rents assessed @ Taka 275 per month from 1-1-1972 to 31-12-1980) and accordingly, the Government demanded payment of balance amount of Taka 24,650 vide Memo No. AHD/Dhaka dated 3-3-1983 and consequently, the petitioner paid the rent. But the petitioner was utterly surprised after receiving a Memo being No. 82(AP)/DA/2009/444 dated 1-6-2003 from the respondent-Government under the signature of respondent No. 5 cancelling the petitioner's appointment as a Caretaker of "China Building" and asking him to vacate his Flat No. 17 within 15 days on the plea of the petitioner being (i) defaulter in payment of rents and also, (ii) living there illegally as he was no longer in the Government service.
